Dear [Student's Name],

I hope this email finds you well. I am writing to address your concern regarding the recorded lectures for HIST 150, which do not have captions. I understand the importance of accessibility for students with disabilities, and I want to assure you that we take this matter seriously.

As you have already established accommodations on file, I would like to inform you that we will work to provide alternative arrangements for the recorded lectures. Our institution's standard protocol for providing accommodations for students with disabilities is outlined in our Accessibility Policy (Section 3.2.1). According to this policy, we will provide captions for recorded lectures upon request.

To facilitate this, I would like to request that you please contact our Disability Services office to confirm your existing accommodations and provide any additional information they may require. They will work with our Instructional Support Services team to arrange for captions to be added to the recorded lectures.

In the meantime, I recommend that you reach out to our Instructional Support Services team to discuss alternative arrangements for accessing the lectures, such as live captioning or a transcript of the lectures. They will be happy to assist you in finding a solution that meets your needs.

Please do not hesitate to contact me if you have any further questions or concerns. I am committed to ensuring that you have equal access to the course materials and can successfully complete HIST 150.

Thank you for bringing this matter to my attention, and I look forward to working with you to find a solution.

Academic Support Services

- Videos must have accurate captions before being assigned.

- Personally identifiable information from education records will not be disclosed without the student's prior written consent, except as permitted by law.
- Directory information may be released unless the student files a request to withhold it within the first 10 calendar days of the term; this request remains in effect until revoked in writing.
- Staff are prohibited from uploading education records to external software services without a signed data-use agreement with the university.

- Must contact the instructor within 14 calendar days of grades being posted if a final course grade is believed to be incorrect.
- Can submit a written appeal to the department chair within 30 calendar days of grades being posted if the issue is not resolved.
- The department chair must provide a written decision within 21 business days of receiving the appeal; the dean's office decision is final.

- Students must attend all scheduled class meetings.
- Unexcused absences exceeding 15% of scheduled meetings may result in a lowered final grade.

- An instructor must notify a student in writing within 10 business days of suspecting academic misconduct.

- A first violation can result in a zero on the assignment, while a second violation leads to referral to the Office of Student Conduct and may result in suspension. Records of violations are kept for 7 years.

- Requests to reschedule one exam due to scheduling conflicts must be submitted at least 14 days before the first day of the final examination period.
- The request should be made to the instructor of the later exam.
- The rescheduled exam must take place during the final examination period.

- A grade of Incomplete can only be assigned if a student has completed at least 70% of the course work with a passing average and is unable to finish due to documented exceptional circumstances.
- The remaining work must be completed by the end of the following semester.
- If the Incomplete is not resolved by the end of the following semester, it will automatically convert to an F.

- Courses can be withdrawn from without a grade until the end of the second week of the semester.
- Withdrawal after the second week but before the eleventh week results in a W grade, which does not impact the GPA.
- Withdrawal after the tenth week requires documented extenuating circumstances and approval from the dean.

- Recordings from remote proctoring software can only be reviewed by the course instructor and authorized academic integrity staff.
- Recordings are deleted 90 days after the end of the term unless they are part of an open misconduct case.
- Students can request to view their own recording within 30 days of the exam.

- Passwords must be at least 14 characters long and do not need to expire unless a compromise is suspected.
- An account is locked for 30 minutes after 10 consecutive failed sign-in attempts.
- Multi-factor authentication is required for all students and employees.
- Suspected password compromises must be reported to the IT Service Desk within 24 hours.

- Courses can be added online until the fifth day of the semester.
- Between the sixth and tenth day, a course can be added with an instructor's signature and a $50 late registration fee.
- No courses can be added after the tenth day of the semester.

- Class recordings can only be shared with enrolled students in the same section and must be deleted from the Learning Management System (LMS) within 30 days after final grades are posted.
- Students are not allowed to record class sessions without instructor permission, except when it is an approved accommodation.

- Syllabi must be posted in the learning management system by the first day of classes.
- Syllabi must include the grading breakdown, instructor's office hours, and the university's disability accommodation statement.
- Changes to the grading breakdown after the second week of the term require written notice to students at least 7 days in advance.

- Complaints not covered by other university policies must first be addressed with the involved staff member or office.
- If unresolved, students must file a written complaint with the Dean of Students within 60 days of the incident.
- The Dean of Students will acknowledge the complaint within 5 business days and provide a written response within 30 business days.

- Generative AI tools can only be used for university work if approved by Information Technology Services.
- Student education records, health information, and Social Security numbers must not be entered into AI tools not hosted on university-managed infrastructure.
- Violations must be reported to the Information Security Office within 2 business days.
